entry.title: Classical Oracle Separation of QMA from the QCMA Hierarchy and Quantum Cryptography Even When P = QCMA
entry.summary:
Remark: This work is in submission at STOC'27 and thus the full manuscript has been publicly posted on the conference website since November 3rd, 2026. Inspired by the Codeword-Hash Structure problem recently introduced by Cakan (arXiV, 2026) to separate $\mathsf{QMA}$ from $\mathsf{QCIP}$, we introduce a new problem called Codeword-Hash pairs in Noise ($\mathsf{CHN}$) and prove that, in the query complexity model, it is in $\mathsf{QMA}$ but hard for the $\mathsf{QCMA}$ hierarchy $\mathsf{QCMAH} = \bigcup_{d\geq1}\mathsf{QCMA}^{\mathsf{QCMA}^{\cdots^{\mathsf{QCMA}}}}$, the classical-witness quantum-verifier analogue of $\mathsf{PH}=\bigcup_{d\ge1}\mathsf{NP}^{\mathsf{NP}^{\cdots^{\mathsf{NP}}}}$. Using this problem, we show that there exists a classical oracle ${O}$ such that $\mathsf{P}^{O}=\mathsf{BQP}^{O}=\mathsf{QCMA}^{O} =\mathsf{QCMAH}^{O} \subset \mathsf{QMA}^{O} \text{ but } \mathsf{QMA}^{O}\not\subseteq\mathsf{QCMAH}^{O},$ thus showing that quantum state or quantum proof advantage could exist even if classical computers can efficiently solve any problem that can be quantumly verified with a classical proof.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #cryptography #combinatorics

entry.title: Package managers have an integrity problem
entry.summary:
I tested 25 of the most popular package managers to check whether they detect a compromised package repository injecting malicious code into legitimate packages. This code integrity problem could be solved using cryptographic hashes or signatures, but many package managers are still vulnerable to this threat. Of the 25 package managers reviewed 1 , fewer than half used lockfiles that checked for tampering by default, and only two verified the integrity of every package they downloaded.

Source: Trail of Bits Security Research · Tags: #infosec #cryptography #rust #databases

entry.title: Succinct Arguments for QMA in the Quantum Random Oracle Model. Succinct arguments are a fundamental cryptographic primitive for verifying computational claims with small communication.
entry.summary:
Succinct arguments are a fundamental cryptographic primitive for verifying computational claims with small communication. In the classical setting, succinct arguments for NP can be constructed from unstructured hardness alone (e.g., hash functions) by compiling probabilistically checkable proofs (PCPs) or interactive oracle proofs (IOPs) for NP via the commit-and-open paradigm. In contrast, known succinct arguments for QMA rely on ``structured'' cryptographic primitives, or on the quantum PCP conjecture.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics

entry.title: Differential Meet-in-the-Middle Attacks on Feistel Ciphers. Differential meet-in-the-middle attacks, introduced by Boura et al.
entry.summary:
Differential meet-in-the-middle attacks, introduced by Boura et al. in 2023, propose a new way of dealing with differential distinguishers. It allows, in particular, to combine differential attacks with initial structures, that were usually used exclusively for meet-in-the-middle attacks.

entry.title: Provable dual attack on LWE via lattice projection
entry.summary:
The Learning with Errors (LWE) problem is a cornerstone of post-quantum cryptography, and the dual attack is a central tool for evaluating its concrete hardness. In provable dual attacks, a major bottleneck is the large number of discrete Gaussian samples required over the dual lattice. While recent works have focused on accelerating the guessing step via modulus switching, the sampling bottleneck has remained largely unoptimized.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum #combinatorics

entry.title: Correlation Power Analysis of SHA-2-Based SLH-DSA
entry.summary:
SLH-DSA repeatedly processes a fixed secret seed together with varying public addresses, making its physical implementation a target for side-channel analysis. We present non-profiled correlation power analysis (CPA) procedures for the address-based pseudorandom function in all six SHA-2-based SLH-DSA parameter sets, using SHA256 compression rounds and message-schedule expansion. The procedures include joint recovery of two partial secrets in the 256-bit parameter sets and an alternative first message-schedule step for 128-bit WOTS+ addresses.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Guess-and-Determine Rebound Revisited: Full Quantum Collision Attack on AES-256 in DM Hash Mode
entry.summary:
At CRYPTO 2025, Qin et al. introduced the guess-and-determine (GD) rebound attack, which integrates the guess-and-determine approach by Bouillaguet, Derbez, and Fouque and the rebound attack by Mendel et al. Taking the GD rebound as a building block, this paper introduces several classical and quantum models to convert the semi-free-start (SFS) collision attack or free-start (FS) collision attack into collision attacks on DM hashing mode with AES. As an application, the first full quantum collision attack on AES-256-DM is proposed.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Codetta: High-Capacity, Keyless, and Undetectable Multi-Agent Collusion. Multi-agent systems powered by large language models (LLMs) achieve strong performance through natural-language collaboration.
entry.summary:
Multi-agent systems powered by large language models (LLMs) achieve strong performance through natural-language collaboration. The same communication channel can also enable collusion, such as exfiltrating confidential data or coordinating unauthorized actions. While auditors inspect transcripts to detect suspicious behavior, steganography could, in principle, evade such audits by concealing covert payloads within ordinary-looking messages.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum #combinatorics
